bug_semantics: When an application programmatically puts attacker-controlled text in a DocumentType publicId, systemId, or internalSubset and serializes it, the serializer concatenates those fields into the DOCTYPE declaration without validating their XML grammar. A quote or '>' can escape a public/system identifier and ']>' can close the internal subset, causing attacker-chosen markup or declarations to be emitted outside the intended DOCTYPE context; a downstream parser with entity expansion can then expose an XXE-class impact.
flaw_origin: Commit 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 made the already-written unsafe DOCTYPE formatter effective by replacing its throwaway local array with writes to the caller's serialization buffer. Its immediate parent 4e759a92ea4dab7e88dbd9317869447629b5f369 constructed the same unchecked text in a new local 'buf' that was never returned or joined, so a DocumentType produced no serialized DOCTYPE there. The introducer is therefore this atomic one-parent buffer-routing change, not the earlier dead formatter text or later moves, formatting changes, and API extensions.
ai_marker: absent: commit 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 has human author and committer jindw <jindw@xidea.org>, an empty commit message, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer, and no bot identity
evidence: The frozen bundle for GHSA-f6ww-3ggp-fr8h / CVE-2026-41674 identifies programmatic DocumentType serialization as the attack path: publicId, systemId, and internalSubset are stored and emitted verbatim; its affected ranges are @xmldom/xmldom <0.8.13 and >=0.9.0,<0.9.10 plus legacy xmldom <=0.6.0.
The CVE.org CVE JSON endpoint returned cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED, GitHub_M as CNA, the same verbatim-DocumentType mechanism, and fixed boundaries 0.8.13 and 0.9.10; it is not rejected or withdrawn.

git show 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 -- dom.js shows the causal hunk in the DOCUMENT_TYPE_NODE branch: it deletes `var buf = ['<!DOCTYPE ',nodeName]` and instead calls `buf.push('<!DOCTYPE ',node.name)`, after which unchecked publicId, systemId, and internalSubset text is appended to the caller-owned output buffer.

Direct parent-tree inspection at 4e759a92ea4dab7e88dbd9317869447629b5f369 shows XMLSerializer.serializeToString creates an outer buffer, calls serializeToString(node, buf), and joins only that outer buffer, while the DocumentType branch shadows it with a new local buffer and never returns or joins the new buffer. Thus the vulnerable emitted-DOCTYPE mechanism is absent in the immediate parent.

git rev-list --parents -n 1 reports `64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 4e759a92ea4dab7e88dbd9317869447629b5f369`: the BIC is a non-merge one-parent commit, so there is no squash/member history to decompose.
git cat-file -p 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 shows author and committer jindw <jindw@xidea.org> and no message or trailers; the BIC commit object contains no AI authorship marker.

git tag --contains 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 begins at 0.1.0, and merge-base checks confirm the BIC is an ancestor of vulnerable tags 0.8.12 and 0.9.9, matching the advisory's historical affected ranges.

The advisory-linked direct fix 372008f9ae0e20fd69f761c7b79e202598267314 adds requireWellFormed checks for PubidLiteral, SystemLiteral, and the internalSubset closing sequence before the existing DOCTYPE concatenation; its parent 7207a4b0e0bcc228868075ed991665ef9f73b1c2 has no such DocumentType checks.

Tag topology closes both maintained lines: 372008f9ae0e20fd69f761c7b79e202598267314 is contained by 0.9.10 but not 0.9.9, while backport 6ca3a416353a4d3143d172c5240c138e296a3258 is contained by 0.8.13 but not 0.8.12.

The fix is explicitly opt-in: requireWellFormed defaults to false, so the advisory tells applications handling untrusted DocumentType fields to pass `{ requireWellFormed: true }`; this limitation does not change the human provenance of the original emitted-field sink.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and publicly confirmed: unvalidated DocumentType fields cross a programmatic input-to-serializer boundary and can terminate or alter the DOCTYPE grammar. History separates dead-looking text from the actual causal first write. Commit 5fb8fb92b2cb9d7c6b8b5477900e90619b14e432 first drafted the unchecked formatter, but it reassigned the helper's buffer parameter to a local array, so its caller joined an unchanged outer array. Commit 64cd7b6e5ef838e98d418d0e90aba5f5db1e4478 is the smallest surviving public commit that routed that unchecked formatter into the returned serialization output; its immediate parent lacks that effective mechanism. Later commits moved/reformatted the sink and expanded internalSubset reachability but did not precede this publicId/systemId/direct-property-write serialization path. The direct fix adds opt-in well-formedness validation and is present at the two patched tag boundaries through the main-line commit and its 0.8 backport. Finally, the BIC commit object is authored and committed by jindw and has neither a bot identity nor any AI/coauthor/generated trailer. Under the BIC-only attribution rule, this real vulnerability is NOT_AI.
